STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square plate with a raised rim band and a flat centre, no inner wall visible. Flat plate, square.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are 20-30 cm. The plate looks medium-sized, not a large platter.
b) Reference: cherry tomatoes are about 3 cm. The plate spans roughly 9-10 tomato lengths across its width (about 280-300 px across versus tomatoes about 30 px), giving about 27-30 cm. Reconciling with the type estimate, I take a width of about 24 cm.

Area = 24 x 24 = 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Tofu cubes: about 9 visible cubes, roughly 2.5 cm each, with a few hidden underneath. Estimate 12 cubes x about 12 g each (2.5 cm cube ≈ 15 ml, tofu about 0.9 g/ml, so about 14 g). Use 12 x 14 = about 170 g. Tofu is spread across roughly 35% of the plate in a low layer, about 2 cm thick at the peak, averaging about 1 cm. Area 0.35 x 576 = 202 cm², x 1.0 cm = 202 ml x 0.9 = about 180 g. Use 175 g.
- Cherry tomatoes: 5 visible, plus about 2 hidden. 7 x 15 g = 105 g.
- Mushrooms (shimeji-type, cooked): spread over about 20% of the plate, 115 cm², thin layer about 1 cm average. 115 ml x 0.6 = about 70 g.
- Oil and seasoning sauce: a light smear, about 0.3 cm over 15% of the plate (86 cm²) = 26 ml x 1.0 = about 25 g.

Total food ≈ 175 + 105 + 70 + 25 = 375 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No separate base layer beyond the sauce smear. Light portion on a large plate, so no extra weight added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (cooked, as served):
- Pan-fried firm tofu: about 150 kcal/100 g (oil absorbed, so slightly higher than plain tofu).
- Cherry tomato: about 18 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked mushrooms: about 35 kcal/100 g.
- Oil/sauce: about 100 kcal/100 g (mostly oil).

Energy: tofu 175 g → 263 kcal; tomato 105 g → 19 kcal; mushroom 70 g → 25 kcal; oil 25 g → 25 kcal. Total ≈ 330 kcal.
